searches.note: Twenty four searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Eight were restricted to a producer's or a wine body's domain (heimann.hu twice, vesztergombi.hu twice, winesofhungary.hu with bor.hu, takler.hu, eszterbauer.hu, vidabor.hu) and read as primary for the house's own dates; the last three returned nothing of use. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on one secondary source or none was cut or hedged.

Sources whose title or address names a living person were met among the results and are cited neither in the fragment nor here; the one such address in the fragment (Decanter's Vida review) was replaced.

tested: Barbár's grapes, the Porkoláb ridge planting of 2002, made only in ripe sound years: heimann.hu product pages, Wine Folly, Bortársaság, Concours Mondial; kept.

1758: heimann.hu family and press pages (a marriage record, the house's claim); kept as the family's account. German descent: the house's press page hosts a critic's article; kept as the family's own account.
The barrel regime: Bortársaság alone, by a second search; kept hedged as one merchant's sheet.
Kadarka clone trial of 2005 with more than thirty clones: an importer's interview whose address names a living person, so not cited; the house page cited by the author stands.
Organic from the mid 2010s: a merchant gives certified conversion from 2020; cut. Barbarossa first in 2022: not borne out as a first; reworded.
The name from Bartók's Allegro barbaro: heimann.hu Barbár pages; added.
changed: story: was the family in Szekszárd since 1758 by its own account; now dated to the marriage record of 1758 the house cites, German descent kept as the family's own account (heimann.hu, the family and press pages, by search).
story: the next generation's training in Germany and France was cut: France has no source, and Geisenheim rests only on an importer's interview whose address names a living person.
story: organic farming from the middle of the 2010s was cut; a merchant gives certified conversion from 2020 and no second source settles it.

story, others: Barbarossa was first made with the 2022 vintage; no source says first, so now joined Barbár in the 2020s as its second wine, listed from 2022 (hungarianwines.eu, Magyar Bor summit listing).
story, label: added that the name comes from Bartók's Allegro barbaro, by the house's account (heimann.hu Barbár pages, by search), with Béla Bartók's dates.
sources: the Wine Folly guide gave way to the Magyar Bor summit listing of Barbarossa 2023.
open: Barbár's barrel regime rests on one merchant's sheet for 2020 (Bortársaság), hedged as such; the house's own 2020 page was not read for it.
The three clone Porkoláb Kadarka in others rests on the house's Heimann & Fiai page alone.

tested: Founded 1996 and the twentieth anniversary in 2016: BBJ, Xpatloop, Hungarian Review; kept. One listing gives 1987; set aside as the author did.
Winemaker of the Year 2004, two sons: Hungarian Review and a second profile; kept.
Regnum Merlot and Cabernet Franc led, five varieties in 2020: a Szekszárd tasting page, kifli.hu listing, Bortársaság; kept.
Taverns, Budapest restaurants, state economy manager, land taken: not found; cut and generalised.
Regnum's oak regime: a search for it returned nothing on Takler; cut.
changed: story: was land taken in the communist years, the founder a manager in the town's state economy, sales to local taverns and then Budapest restaurants; none of these was found in this check, so now the district's vineyards and cellars passed to the state and the founder set up his own winery in 1996 (Hungarian Review, BBJ).

wine.making: was tank fermentation and about a year and a half in Hungarian and French oak, made only in strong vintages, from one merchant's sheet; no second source or house sheet was found, so now raised in oak with the figures left out.
table: made only in strong years was cut for the same reason; now Cabernet Sauvignon beside the two leaders.
story: Kékfrankos and Syrah joining the blend now told as in later vintages, from the 2020 listing of five varieties.
open: Regnum's barrel regime and its being made only in strong vintages are unsourced beyond one merchant; the integrator may restore them if a house sheet is found.

tested: 1746 and ten generations: parlament.hu and hungarianwines.eu; kept.
Nagyapám from clone trials and selected old vines, named for a forebear who owned vineyards: parlament.hu (2023 page); kept and the label reworded.
Steel alone for 2024: wineparis.bor.hu; kept. Own yeasts: not found; cut.
Plots in Bodzás, Görögszó, Porkoláb valley and Palánki hill: parlament.hu, hungarianwines.eu; kept.
Sógor and Báró Steiner: hungarianwines.eu (rebranding article), Magyar Bor summit listings; detail cut to what they bear.
Settlers, Benedictines, Kadarka's rise and fall, phylloxera 1875 or 1886: four regional guides; the abbots' tax relief not found and cut.
changed: story: was tax relief from the Benedictine abbots in the early eighteenth century; no source found, so now Hungarian and German settlers replanted the hills after the Ottoman wars.

story: was Kadarka replanted widely after phylloxera; now the district's flagship grape in the nineteenth century, then losing ground to Kékfrankos and the Bordeaux varieties over the twentieth (Taste Hungary and Offbeat Budapest guides, by search).
story, label: was labels carrying grandparents and great grandparents of the town's old middle class; now the Parliament page's tribute to a forebear who owned vineyards in the town.
wine.making: fermentation with its own yeasts cut (not borne out); the 2016's steel and oak hedged as one importer's account.
others: Sógor's own yeasts and steel, and Báró Steiner's twelve months in 500 litre barrels, cut for want of a second source; báró glossed as baron.
open: One summit listing gives 2010 as the winery's founding; founded stays empty because no second source agrees.

tested: Winemaker of the Year 2011: Trademagazin and Best of Budapest; kept.
Founded: 1989, 1990 and 1995 in three listings; left empty and the story reworded.
The daughter back from New Zealand for the 2020 harvest: Wines of Hungary magazine; kept, the son's replanting not found and cut.
Valles grapes and casks, cold soak and fermentation: Wines of Hungary Wine Paris listing for 2020; kept and the soak added.
Bikavér rules: hungarianwines.eu regulation pages and Magyar Bor; a year in oak for both tiers, Kékfrankos at least 45 per cent and Kadarka required; no bottle year or yield rule for Prémium found.
Garay's song of 1846 and the communist era loss of the name, regained late in the 1980s: Magyar Bor, Decanter and two guides; kept.
changed: wine.grapes: Merlot about a quarter cut; it rests on one critic's note for 2020.

wine.making, label, story: was the Prémium rule of lower yields and a year in bottle; no source bears out either, the year in oak holds for both tiers, so now every Bikavér must spend at least a year in oak (hungarianwines.eu regulation, Magyar Bor).
wine.making: the cold soak and cool fermentation added from the Wines of Hungary listing for 2020.
wine.label: Szekszárdi Bikavér's at least four grapes cut, since Magyar Bor and the 2016 rules differ; Kékfrankos led with Kadarka required stands.
story: was the turn of the 1990s; listings give 1989, 1990 and 1995, so now the years after the change of 1989.
story: the son's replanting and new cellar and the father keeping to the vineyards cut (not found); the daughter's return from New Zealand for the 2020 harvest kept (Wines of Hungary magazine).
others: Hidaspetre's fifteen months and Tündértánc cut for want of sources; Petit Bonsai Kadarka added from the Magyar Bor Wine Paris listing.
sources: the Decanter review, whose address carries the founder's living name, gave way to hungarianwines.eu's Bikavér regulation page.
traps: Kadarka's requirement in Szekszárd's Bikavér added beside the tiers.
open: The Prémium tier's exact Kékfrankos minimum is given as 35 and 45 per cent in different Magyar Bor pages; the record teaches no figure.

tested: Founded 1991 on vines and a Kadarka Street cellar returned after privatisation: vesztergombi.hu family page and hungarianwines.eu; kept.
Winemaker of the Year 1993: hungarianwines.eu list and the house; kept.
First vineyard judge: the house names György Vesztergombi with no tie or dates; told as the house names it.
Porkolábvölgy Kékfrankos 2019, 24 months in 300 to 500 litre barrels: Wines of Hungary listing; kept.

St. László Bikavér, patron saint, 24 months new 300 and 500 litre oak and six months in bottle, Parliament's Bikavér category with the 2019: parlament.hu, Hungary Today, Wines of Hungary; kept and set right.
Sebestyén in the Porkoláb valley: not found; replaced by Eszterbauer.
changed: story: was a forebear who served as first vineyard judge and brought a formal register; the house names a György Vesztergombi as the first vineyard judge with no tie or dates, so now the house names a Vesztergombi, and the office is told as the house tells it.
story: was a new winery on Borkút Street where the reds are aged; now its cellar later on Borkút Street (hungarianwines.eu).
story, others: St. László Bikavér now named for the town's patron saint and the winner of the Parliament's Bikavér category with the 2019 (parlament.hu, Hungary Today).
others: the Kadarka's two years in steel and oak cut (one listing).
traps: Sebestyén, not found in the Porkoláb valley, gave way to Eszterbauer, whose plots there the Parliament page names.
wine.serve: was 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; now 15 to 17, the Codex's medium red, as for the group's other Kékfrankos led wine.
open: Whether Porkolábvölgy Kékfrankos is the house's flagship stays open: St. László Bikavér is its Parliament winner; the swap is refused here for the group's balance (see the review).
The label prints Porkolábvölgy; wine.name keeps the plan's Porkoláb-völgy form for the integrator to settle.

living_names_met: The Heimann father, mother and son, named on heimann.hu and an importer's interview.
The Takler founder and his two sons, named in the Hungarian Review, BBJ and Xpatloop.
The Eszterbauer head of the family and two winemakers, named on parlament.hu and hungarianwines.eu.

The Vida founder and his daughter, named in Trademagazin, Best of Budapest and the Wines of Hungary magazine; the founder's name is also the house's legal name and sits in Decanter's and Magyar Bor's addresses.
The Vesztergombi founder and his son, named on vesztergombi.hu and parlament.hu.
A British critic whose name is in tasting addresses and on the Heimann press file.
people_note: None of these is named in the fragment; none is yet in people.json. The read together agent may add them by role. The Vesztergombi first vineyard judge is historic but undated and is not named.

swaps.proposed: The author raised a change of Vesztergombi's flagship from the Porkoláb valley Kékfrankos to St. László Bikavér.
swaps.ruling: Refused. St. László Bikavér is the house's Parliament category winner and its leading blend, but the group already teaches a Prémium Szekszárdi Bikavér in Vida's Valles, and the Porkolábvölgy Kékfrankos is a real single vineyard wine of the house (Wines of Hungary listing for 2019) that teaches Szekszárd's leading grape on one site; St. László stays first among the others. The question of which wine leads the house is left open for the integrator.

codex_tension: The plan's why for Takler and the region summary speak of Bordeaux variety reds carrying the district abroad; no fact in tension.

The plan's why for Vesztergombi (cellars in the old lanes of the town) fits the Kadarka Street cellar of 1991, but the house's cellar is later on Borkút Street; the read together agent may soften the why.
The plan's note for Takler asks Primarius Merlot and the Gurovica Kékfrankos among the others; neither was sourced twice, so the record keeps Örökség and the Szenta hill Kékfrankos.
The region summary says Szekszárd's Bikavér rules are stricter on the native grapes; consistent with the Kékfrankos and Kadarka minimums found.
